trial_info.title: A Phase I/Ib Global, Multicenter, Open-label Umbrella Study Evaluating the Safety and Efficacy of Targeted Therapies in Subpopulations of Patients With Metastatic Colorectal Cancer (INTRINSIC)

patient_to_trial_evaluation.reasoning: The patient is 52 years old, has metastatic colorectal cancer, ECOG performance status of 1, and is newly diagnosed (treatment-naïve for targeted therapies). She is willing to undergo molecular profiling. Her creatinine and bilirubin levels require further clarification (see missing information below). The presence of the KRAS G13D mutation makes her potentially eligible, depending on the specific targeted therapies being investigated in the trial and whether they are relevant to her mutation. Active brain metastases are not present. Cardiac history is not mentioned, so we're assuming no severe cardiac conditions. The ECOG status is acceptable. The patient is female, so pregnancy/breastfeeding is not applicable. The AST, ALT and Alkaline Phosphatase are elevated, potentially indicating liver involvement of the metastatic disease and will need to be monitored. But these elevations don't necessarily exclude her immediately as bilirubin is normal. The low Hgb of 10.2 should be addressed before enrolling in the trial.
inclusion_criteria_met: No prior treatment with targeted therapy for current disease
exclusion_criteria_status: Active brain metastases - No active brain metastases
